newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway debt tracks Bunds, crown firms slightly.
newsitem.headline: Norway debt tracks Bunds, crown firms slightly.

text.p: The Norwegian crown firmed slightly and short rates were largely static in thin activity.
Several stoppages to systems at the Oslo stock exchange caused disruptions to trade and dampened activity, dealers said.
Long-bond yields rose marginally in line with movements in Germany and the 10-year yield spread with Bunds was unchanged.

In a new forecast, Handelsbanken Markets said it expected the crown to continue to weaken for the remainder of the year and for Norges Bank to react by tightening monetary policy by raising short-term interest rates.

Handelsbanken projected the crown to fall to around 104.50 against the inverse European Currency Unit (ECU) index over the next six months. The crown is currently fluctuating between 101.80 and 102 versus the index.
"As the crown continues to weaken, Norges Bank eventually should see fit to raise short-term rates again, for example, when the ECU index passes 104," it said.
It added that any rate hike should encourage investors to move into shorter domestic maturities, causing the 10-year spread against Germany to eventually widen out to 100 basis points.
"Even if we were to take a more optimistic view of Norwegian inflation than our macro forecast and instead expect, say 2.5 percent, that is still 100 basis points above German inflation.
"In this context, we do not believe a spread of 10-30 basis points can persist," the report said.

Furthermore the German Bundesbank is expected to raise its rates in reaction to the weak but steady, export-led recovery sometime after the end of 1997. This would lead Norges Bank to follow suit, it said.
"A total increase in the Norwegian short rate of 125 points thus does not seem unreasonable," Handelsbanken said.
The bank revised downwards its estimate for 1997 inflation to 2.7 percent from 3.2 percent and lowered its forecast for wage growth to 4.2 percent from 4.5 percent.
However, it estimated inflation to grow by 3.7 percent in 1998 and by 4.3 percent in 1999.
